bugLogs.title: Low contrast on payment hint text in checkout
affected_users: older users with declining contrast sensitivity
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the checkout payment page
Locate the paragraph with class 'hint' containing the text 'We never store your card details'
Observe the text color is #c4c4c4 on a #ffffff background
Measure the contrast ratio using a color contrast tool
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The text should have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background color to meet WCAG 2.1 AA requirements for normal-sized text.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The text has a contrast ratio of only 1.74:1 (foreground #c4c4c4 on background #ffffff), which is significantly below the required 4.5:1 threshold.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: In the CSS rule for p, change color from #c4c4c4 to #767676 (4.54:1 on #ffffff; measured 1.74:1, required 4.5:1).

_severity_override.rule: CLAUDE.md: checkout flow violations are always critical

bugLogs.title: Missing accessible name on payment image button
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the checkout payment page
Use a screen reader to inspect the element's accessible name
Observe that no name is announced for the control
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The image button should have a programmatically determinable accessible name that describes its purpose, such as 'Pay Now', so assistive technologies can identify the control.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The input[type="image"] element has no alt attribute, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or associated label, resulting in no accessible name being exposed to assistive technologies.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add alt='Pay Now' to the input[type="image"] element. Example: <input type="image" src="pay-now.png" width="120" height="40" alt="Pay Now">

bugLogs.title: Promo code select element missing accessible name
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the checkout payment page
Locate the promo code dropdown menu
Use a screen reader to inspect the element with id 'promo'
Observe that no accessible name is announced for the select element
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The select element should have an accessible name that programmatically identifies its purpose, such as 'Promo code', so assistive technologies can announce it to users.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The select element with id 'promo' has no associated label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title attribute, leaving it unnamed for assistive technologies.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add a visible label associated with the select element: <label for="promo">Promo code</label> placed before the select. Alternatively, add aria-label="Promo code" to the select element.

bugLogs.title: Payment form inputs rely on placeholder text instead of persistent labels
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the checkout payment page
Locate the 'Name on card' input field (#pay-name)
Observe that the only text identifying the field is the placeholder
Click into the field and begin typing
Observe that the placeholder text disappears, leaving no visible label
Repeat the process for the 'Card number' input field (#pay-card)
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each form input should have a persistent, visible label that remains visible regardless of whether the field is focused or contains text, per WCAG 3.3.2.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The inputs #pay-name and #pay-card rely solely on placeholder text for identification. The placeholder disappears when the user begins typing, leaving no visible label to identify the field.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add visible <label> elements associated with each input using the 'for' attribute. For example: <label for="pay-name">Name on card</label> before <input type="text" id="pay-name">, and <label for="pay-card">Card number</label> before <input type="text" id="pay-card">. Remove the placeholder attributes or keep them as supplementary hints only.
